title: Azgor or King Izgadar
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a king of Persia in the time of Rav Ashi, and he loved and honored the sages of Israel. See Zevachim 19a: Rav Ashi said, Huna bar Natan told me, 'Once I was standing before King Azgader, and he was lifting my belt for me.' And in Ketubot 61a: Ameimar, Mar Zutra, and Rav Ashi were standing at the gate of the house of King Azgor.

There was also a King Izgadar who was wicked, in the time of Mar bar Rav Ashi, as brought in the letter of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 4. He was the grandson of the first, as the Gaon S. Y. Rapoport discussed at length, with good reason and knowledge, in his book Erekh Milin.

notes.text: The Azgor, Azgader and Izgadar spellings and the two kings’ grandfather–grandson relationship are Hyman’s report. No modern regnal identity is supplied.

The consulted Zevachim 19a directly names Izgaddar and Huna bar Natan in the belt episode. This does not establish a modern regnal identity or the two kings’ grandfather–grandson relation. The exact Iggeret and Erekh Milin claims remain attributed to Hyman.
